THE TASK BEHIND THE MAP

What is a geospatial use case?

A geospatial use case is a real-world question that depends on location, distance, spatial relationships, terrain, environmental conditions, networks or change over space. The answer usually requires a combination of data, GIS operations, assumptions, validation and a map or analytical output—not just a single GIS tool.

In GriidAi, the user defines the question, brings or discovers relevant data, reviews the proposed plan, approves supported analysis, validates the result and decides how the output should be used.

01
Site Selection / Compare

Which candidate locations deserve deeper review?

Make candidate locations, constraints, surrounding conditions, proximity relationships and approved scoring criteria explicit. Compare the evidence using a method your team can inspect.

AEC & EnvironmentalLocation & Portfolio
Data, method & outputs +

Compare candidate locations with criteria your team can review

Typical inputs
Candidate locations, constraints, context layers and explicit criteria.
Result to inspect
Comparative map, location metrics and a shortlist for deeper review.
Review point
Review thresholds, units, exclusions and any scoring or weighting logic. A shortlist supports expert judgment; it does not automatically choose the best site.

02
Coverage Gap Analysis / Find gaps

Where is service, access or facility coverage insufficient?

Compare facilities with the people, assets or areas they are intended to serve. Keep the coverage method, service threshold and relevant demand context visible.

Utilities & InfrastructureLocation & Portfolio
Data, method & outputs +

Find where service or access may be insufficient

Typical inputs
Facility locations, a study area, demand or population data and a defined coverage threshold.
Result to inspect
Coverage and gap map, affected areas and contextual summaries.
Review point
Straight-line buffers and network service areas answer different questions. Use the supported method explicitly; a coverage result is not an emergency-response guarantee.

03
Flood & Coastal Risk / Assess scenarios

Which locations may be exposed under a defined flood or coastal scenario?

Screen locations against a named hazard or water-level condition. Review the scenario, geography, period, elevation context and overlay logic before interpreting the exposure result.

Climate ResilienceUtilities & InfrastructureLocation & Portfolio
Data, method & outputs +

Screen locations against a defined flood or coastal scenario

Typical inputs
A defined scenario or hazard layer, assets or locations, AOI and relevant terrain context.
Result to inspect
Scenario exposure map, affected locations and supporting tables.
Review point
Scenario-based exposure is screening evidence. It is not a prediction of exact flooding, catastrophe-loss estimation, asset-failure probability or engineering certification.

04
Hydrology Analysis / Understand terrain / flow

How does water move across the terrain in this study area?

Start with a digital elevation model and a study area. Inspect the raster, review supported terrain and drainage steps, and validate derived flow or stream-network outputs.

AEC & EnvironmentalClimate ResilienceUtilities & Infrastructure
Data, method & outputs +

Turn elevation data into terrain and drainage evidence

Typical inputs
Digital elevation model, study area and appropriate terrain-processing parameters.
Result to inspect
Flow and drainage layers, stream network and related analytical maps.
Review point
Check CRS, elevation units, resolution, NoData and depression handling. Review thresholds and compare drainage patterns with known terrain context.
Explore DEM Hydrology & Stream Network example ↗Bring Your Own Data ↗
05
Vegetation & NDVI / Measure

Where is vegetation condition higher, lower or changing across the study area?

Use suitable red and near-infrared raster inputs to calculate a vegetation index. Keep imagery dates, required bands, quality constraints and interpretation connected to the result.

AEC & EnvironmentalClimate Resilience
Data, method & outputs +

Use satellite imagery to examine vegetation condition

Typical inputs
Compatible red and near-infrared imagery, study area and a relevant time period.
Result to inspect
NDVI raster, a readable map legend and contextual summaries where supported.
Review point
Verify band meaning, alignment, clouds and NoData. NDVI alone does not establish crop yield, biomass, a plant-health diagnosis or causation.

05 / DATA + METHOD

The same question can produce a different answer when the data or method changes

Coverage & time

A historical observation, forecast, scenario and current snapshot are different kinds of evidence. Confirm geographic and temporal coverage.

Resolution & spatial reference

Scale, CRS, distance units, raster alignment and missing values affect the result. Absence of data is not automatically zero.

Thresholds & rights

Make distance, scenario and scoring assumptions visible. Check licensing and attribution before exporting or publishing.

Explore Data & Formats ↗
06 / EXPERT CONTROL

AI can help organize the analysis. Experts still control the method and result.

AI proposes the work. Experts control what proceeds.

A plausible map can still be wrong when the projection, time window, units, selected data or analytical assumption is wrong. Review the plan before processing and validate the mapped or tabular result before using it.
